1. Executive Summary

This report documents a working, runnable prototype of Nayi Disha (WasteLoop): a TypeScript/Fastify backend, a PostgreSQL database (via Prisma), a minimal React dashboard, and a real routing engine (OSRM), implementing the full citizen-facing loop — scan → AI classify → time-limited token → triple-lock verification at a bin → reward release — plus the municipal side: simulated IoT sensor telemetry, an admin command center, and dynamic multi-stop route optimization for collection vehicles.

14/14 backend smoke tests passing 0 npm audit vulnerabilities Real OSRM road-network routing Full golden path verified in-browser

Scope of this prototype

✅ Fully implemented

  • Accounts, JWT + bcrypt auth, role-based access (citizen / admin)
  • Full scan → token → triple-lock → throw → reward chain, including anti-gaming failure paths (expired token, GPS mismatch, missing evidence)
  • Sensor telemetry ingestion, history storage, and a device-auth contract that a real device can use unmodified
  • Real road-network route optimization via self-hosted/public OSRM + a nearest-neighbor + 2-opt heuristic
  • Admin analytics: ward summaries, segregation trends, fleet status
  • Rewards ledger, badges, and redemption catalog

🔶 Intentionally mocked / deferred

  • AI waste classification: deterministic hash-based mock behind a swappable interface (no vision model / API key wired up yet)
  • Raspberry Pi / ESP32 hardware: not physically connected — a software simulator posts to the exact same endpoints a real device would use
  • MQTT transport: sensor ingestion uses plain authenticated HTTP POST instead, for simplicity in this prototype phase

The remainder of this report covers the implementation architecture, the database schema, the API surface, and screenshots of every major screen exercised during end-to-end verification.

2. Implementation Architecture

This extends the conceptual process diagram in dustbin_arch.md with the concrete system components built for this prototype: a Fastify backend organized as one module per domain concern, a single PostgreSQL database via Prisma, and OSRM as the real routing engine behind the route optimizer.

graph TD subgraph CLIENT["Client — React + Vite SPA"] FE["Dashboard / Scan / Bins / Throw /\nRewards / Admin / Routes pages\nTailwind · React Query · Leaflet · Recharts"] end subgraph API["Fastify Backend (TypeScript, /api/v1)"] AUTH["Auth\nJWT + bcrypt"] BINS["Bins"] SENS["Sensors\n+ Simulator"] SCAN["Scans\nMock AI classifier"] THROW["Throws\nTriple-lock verification"] REW["Rewards"] ROUTE["Routes\nNearest-neighbor + 2-opt"] ADM["Admin analytics"] end DB[("PostgreSQL\nvia Prisma")] OSRM[("OSRM routing engine\nContraction Hierarchies")] DEVICE["Real ESP32 / Raspberry Pi\n(future) — or simulator today"] FE -- "JWT bearer" --> AUTH FE --> BINS FE --> SCAN FE --> THROW FE --> REW FE --> ROUTE FE --> ADM DEVICE -- "x-device-api-key\n(per-bin secret)" --> SENS AUTH --> DB BINS --> DB SENS --> DB SCAN --> DB THROW --> DB REW --> DB ROUTE --> DB ADM --> DB ROUTE -- "/table /route /nearest" --> OSRM
Hardware-ready by design: every bin has a unique deviceApiKey. Telemetry ingestion is authenticated via an x-device-api-key header — not the citizen JWT — so a real ESP32/Raspberry Pi can POST to /api/v1/bins/:binId/telemetry and /api/v1/bins/:binId/camera-events with zero backend changes. The in-process simulator used for this demo calls the identical code path.

3. Database Design

The schema mirrors the process's own state machine rather than one overloaded table, so anti-gaming failure paths (expired tokens, GPS mismatches, unverified throws) are first-class, queryable states — not just error responses.

erDiagram USER ||--o{ WASTESCAN : creates USER ||--o{ DISPOSALTOKEN : owns USER ||--o{ REWARDTRANSACTION : accrues USER ||--o{ REDEMPTION : requests USER ||--o{ USERBADGE : earns BADGE ||--o{ USERBADGE : "awarded as" REDEMPTIONOPTION ||--o{ REDEMPTION : "redeemed via" WARD ||--o{ BIN : contains BIN ||--o{ SENSORLOG : reports BIN ||--o{ BINCAMERAEVENT : captures BIN ||--o{ THROWEVENT : receives BIN ||--o{ ROUTESTOP : "visited in" SENSORLOG ||--o{ BINCAMERAEVENT : "may trigger" WASTESCAN ||--|| DISPOSALTOKEN : issues DISPOSALTOKEN ||--|| THROWEVENT : "consumed by" THROWEVENT ||--o{ REWARDTRANSACTION : releases ROUTE ||--o{ ROUTESTOP : contains USER { string id PK string email UK string passwordHash Role role int wasteCoinBalance int currentStreak } BIN { string id PK string code UK "fixed QR payload" float latitude float longitude float currentFillPercent BinStatus status string deviceApiKey UK } SENSORLOG { string id PK string binId FK float fillPercent float weightKg datetime recordedAt } WASTESCAN { string id PK string userId FK WasteClassification aiClassification int pendingPoints } DISPOSALTOKEN { string id PK string code UK TokenStatus status datetime expiresAt } THROWEVENT { string id PK VerificationMethod verificationMethod boolean qrMatched boolean throwVerified int pointsAwarded } ROUTE { string id PK float totalDistanceMeters float totalDurationSeconds string algorithm }

Indexes worth noting: SensorLog(binId, recordedAt) for fast time-series reads, RewardTransaction(userId, createdAt) for the ledger view, and unique constraints on Bin.code / Bin.deviceApiKey / DisposalToken.code to make the QR-and-token contract enforceable at the database level.

8. Routing Algorithm

The route optimizer mirrors how a production system (Google Maps / OR-Tools style) would approach multi-stop vehicle routing, split into two concerns:

Real-world distances

  • Candidate bins are selected by explicit ID list or by a fill-percent threshold (ROUTE_FILL_THRESHOLD_PERCENT)
  • OSRM's /table endpoint returns a true road-network distance/duration matrix (Contraction Hierarchies), not straight-line estimates
  • OSRM's /route then produces the actual driving geometry for map rendering

Visit ordering (TSP heuristic)

  • Nearest-neighbor construction gives a fast initial tour
  • 2-opt local search iteratively removes crossing edges to shorten the tour — the same family of technique OR-Tools' guided local search builds on
  • Result is persisted as a Route + ordered RouteStop rows, with per-leg distance/duration

OSRM_BASE_URL is configurable — the prototype defaults to the public OSRM demo server for zero-setup development, with a one-time script (infra/osrm/scripts/fetch_and_prepare_osm.sh) to preprocess a small Central-Delhi OSM extract for a self-hosted instance via Docker Compose.
